summary: Good news if you live in Dallas: we checked the full city code, and Dallas is no stricter than Texas. Dallas bans only a specific list of dangerous and exotic animals (Sec. 7-6.1: dangerous wild animals per Texas Health & Safety Code 822.101 plus margay, badger, wolf, dingo, elephant, primates, crocodilians, venomous reptiles, etc.). Rats are not on that list, and Dallas sets no pet limit on rodents. A pet roof rat is allowed, the same as Texas. The only 'rat' mention in the code is about pest-control traps, not pet keeping.

keep.why: Dallas City Code ch. 7. The prohibited-animals list (Sec. 7-6.1) is dangerous/exotic species only and does not include rats; rodents are kept as pets with no numeric limit. The sole code reference to 'rats' concerns traps for pest control. Not stricter than Texas.
keep.governing_law: Dallas City Code ch. 7, Sec. 7-6.1 (Prohibited animals; rats not listed); no Texas state restriction.

breed.why: No local rodent-breeding restriction or pet-rat cap; Texas imposes no state restriction.
breed.governing_law: Dallas City Code ch. 7, Sec. 7-6.1 (Prohibited animals; rats not listed); no Texas state restriction.

sell_give.why: No local restriction on giving or selling a pet rat; Texas state rules apply.
sell_give.governing_law: Dallas City Code ch. 7, Sec. 7-6.1 (Prohibited animals; rats not listed); no Texas state restriction.

transport.why: No local transport restriction on a pet rat; Texas state rules apply.
transport.governing_law: Dallas City Code ch. 7, Sec. 7-6.1 (Prohibited animals; rats not listed); no Texas state restriction.
